facts.raw_span: A 56-year-old man presented with a 2-month history of bitemporal hemianopia and left labial numbness
visual impairment, bitemporal hemianopia, and right abducens nerve palsy

Pituitary MRI demonstrated diffuse swelling of the pituitary body and stalk, a 7-mm poorly enhancing mass in the right anterior lobe, loss of the posterior pituitary bright spot on T1-weighted images, and thickening of the sphenoid sinus mucosa
Serum IgG4 was elevated at 319 mg/dL
A 56-year-old man presented with a 2-month history of bitemporal hemianopia and left labial numbness
visual impairment, bitemporal hemianopia, and right abducens nerve palsy

Pituitary MRI demonstrated diffuse swelling of the pituitary body and stalk, a 7-mm poorly enhancing mass in the right anterior lobe, loss of the posterior pituitary bright spot on T1-weighted images, and thickening of the sphenoid sinus mucosa
Serum IgG4 was elevated at 319 mg/dL

concepts.why: The combination of hypopituitarism, elevated IgG4 levels, and pituitary MRI findings is consistent with IgG4-related hypophysitis.
The pituitary MRI findings, including diffuse swelling and loss of the posterior pituitary bright spot, could be consistent with lymphocytic hypophysitis.
The 7-mm poorly enhancing mass in the right anterior lobe on pituitary MRI could represent a pituitary adenoma.
The combination of pituitary involvement and thickening of the sphenoid sinus mucosa could be consistent with sarcoidosis.
The pituitary MRI findings, including diffuse swelling and loss of the posterior pituitary bright spot, could be consistent with tubercular hypophysitis.
The combination of pituitary involvement and thickening of the sphenoid sinus mucosa could be consistent with granulomatosis with polyangiitis.
The elevated IgG4 levels and systemic imaging findings, including a nodular lesion in the left lung field, are consistent with IgG4-related disease.
The laboratory studies demonstrate multiple pituitary hormone deficiencies, consistent with hypopituitarism.
The pituitary MRI findings, including diffuse swelling and loss of the posterior pituitary bright spot, could be consistent with pituitary apoplexy.
The pituitary MRI findings, including diffuse swelling and loss of the posterior pituitary bright spot, could be consistent with Langerhans cell histiocytosis.

rationales.F11: Pituitary MRI findings are consistent with hypophysitis, particularly the diffuse swelling and loss of the posterior pituitary bright spot.
rationales.F12: Elevated IgG4 levels are a hallmark of IgG4-related disease, including IgG4-related hypophysitis.

frontier_selector.rationale: Elevated IgG4 levels and pituitary MRI findings of diffuse swelling and a poorly enhancing mass, along with systemic imaging suggesting IgG4-related disease, support the diagnosis of IgG4-related hypophysitis.
